gen-dafont-disorder-gf-mozilla-headline: Loose, jumpy letters up top. Disorder sprawls with big lowercase and wide gaps, while Mozilla Headline stays friendly in a plain sans, its heavy-bodied letters settling things down.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-mozilla-text: Mozilla Text reads tall and sturdy, its flared terminals easy to follow. Disorder runs rough and scattered above it, and the two sit together like a shouted headline followed by someone speaking steadily.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-nata-sans: Nata Sans reads clean and spacious, with a big central band and curves left open at the mouth. Disorder is the one to make noise with, and Nata Sans is the one to carry the actual words.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-nobile: Every stroke in Disorder is cut at the same gauge, with no swelling at the joins, and it looks rough anyway. Nobile follows with a plain sans feel, caps sitting close to the lowercase, so a long passage moves along smoothly.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-nokora: Nokora lays down a thick, dark stripe of lowercase, with an s that never pinches shut. Nokora feels sturdy and friendly beside Disorder, which looks scrappy, spaced out and a bit unruly by comparison.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-kufi-arabic: Noto Kufi Arabic reads open and tidy, its c showing a welcoming gap and its capitals barely above the lowercase. Noto Kufi Arabic would feel lost if Disorder's pen-like line were made small, so keep that heading big and let the sans stay modest.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans: Disorder arrives with big lowercase, wide-set glyphs and tails as thick as its stems. And Noto Sans, with its tall bodies and open c, is the quiet counterweight that makes the pair feel deliberate.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-adlam: Disorder draws everything as true monoline, with curves that carry no stress and letters spaced well apart. A larger heading size gives it room.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-adlam-u: Noto Sans Adlam Unjoined reads modern and steady, with curve ends held clear of the stem and little height gap between cases. And Disorder's wild, stressless curves are the pair's sharpest tension, rough against tidy.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-anatoli: Disorder never varies its stroke weight, and it still looks raw. Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs, with outward-pointing terminals and a tall x-height, makes the sharpest difference: a scrawl set against something composed.
